correctedCritiques.pro-reason-mathematics-freedom: Strongest feature: The move combines rational normativity, mathematical objectivity, and freedom into a challenge asking whether material processes can ground truth-directed cognition, abstract structure, and accountable agency. Principal limitation: It compresses distinct philosophical problems, leaving randomness, matter, mind, mathematical truth, rational reliability, and freedom inadequately defined or connected, while asserting incompatibilities beyond its supporting argument. Live burden: The case must separate causation from grounding, show why material systems cannot instantiate reliable reasoning, distinguish mathematical discovery from mental production, and defend freedom against naturalistic alternatives. Locked score: The weak band recognizes an important explanatory agenda but reflects severe compression, conceptual instability, limited evidence, uncharitable treatment of differentiated rivals, and no demonstration that theism specifically supplies a superior account.
correctedCritiques.con-autonomy-against-divine-permission: Strongest feature: The reply frames a substantial autonomy objection through constitutional separation of civic authority from theology, giving resistance to supernatural ownership an independent normative dimension. Principal limitation: It leaps from institutional religious freedom to rejecting divine permission, equating metaphysical dependence with political ownership without showing that every theistic relationship extinguishes voluntary allegiance or civic liberty. Live burden: The objection must identify which doctrines transform creation into domination, distinguish ultimate accountability from coercive governance, and explain why supernatural dependence necessarily compromises agency rather than enabling it. Locked score: The mixed band recognizes concern about compulsory obedience, but reflects incomplete contact with the earlier explanatory inference, broad theological generalization, and an autonomy conclusion stronger than its civic evidence.
